evidence.claim: AMLO announced a five-year world truce proposal that would suspend military actions, nuclear tests, and missile tests and create a mediation committee for Ukraine.
evidence.title: Discurso del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador durante el desfile cívico militar: 212 Aniversario de la Independencia
evidence.excerpt: AMLO announced a five-year world truce proposal that would suspend military actions, nuclear tests, and missile tests and create a mediation committee for Ukraine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential transcript with date and first-person ruler statement.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 ruler-period statement with precise date.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct AMLO statement and proposal; the foreign ministry was assigned to present it at the UN.
contrary_evidence: It is a proposal rather than an implemented policy or treaty.
It does not show command over nuclear forces because Mexico has none.

evidence.claim: Mexico warned that a nuclear accident at Zaporizhzhia would have unacceptable humanitarian and environmental consequences and called for a security perimeter around the plant.
evidence.title: Fighting at Ukraine Nuclear Power Site Irresponsible, against Geneva Conventions, Under-Secretary-General Tells Security Council
evidence.excerpt: Mexico warned that a nuclear accident at Zaporizhzhia would have unacceptable humanitarian and environmental consequences and called for a security perimeter around the plant.
evidence.source_locator: Mexico intervention in the Security Council emergency meeting on attacks
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN meeting coverage with an attributed Mexico intervention on nuclear-site risk.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect state attribution through Mexico's UN mission; useful as a ruler-period foreign-policy signal rather than direct nuclear command.
contrary_evidence: The evidence concerns a crisis abroad, not Mexican nuclear infrastructure.
It does not demonstrate internal command-and-control reform.

evidence.claim: Mexico said non-nuclear-weapon States fulfill disarmament commitments without getting anything in return except a vision of potential annihilation, and that the claim nuclear weapons guarantee security is unsustainable and immoral.
evidence.title: Non-Nuclear-Armed States Get Nothing in Return for Fulfilling Commitments Except Threat of Potential Annihilation, First Committee Told
evidence.excerpt: Mexico said non-nuclear-weapon States fulfill disarmament commitments without getting anything in return except a vision of potential annihilation, and that the claim nuclear weapons guarantee security is unsustainable and immoral.
evidence.source_locator: First Committee thematic segment on nuclear weapons
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UN official meeting record summarizing an attributed Mexico intervention.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and squarely on nuclear-risk responsibility.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect state attribution through Mexico's permanent mission; relevant to AMLO as the government's external posture.
contrary_evidence: This is normative advocacy, not proof of domestic safety governance.
It does not by itself show concrete risk reduction at home.

evidence.claim: An IAEA team completed a review of long-term operational safety at the Laguna Verde Nuclear Power Plant in 2022.
evidence.title: IAEA Concludes Long Term Operational Safety Review at Mexico’s Laguna Verde Nuclear Power Plant
evidence.excerpt: An IAEA team completed a review of long-term operational safety at the Laguna Verde Nuclear Power Plant in 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: IAEA news metadata is official and dated, though the page is an index entry rather than a full article.
evidence.period_fit: Excellent 2022 period fit for civilian nuclear safety context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional safety context; at most indirectly attributable to the AMLO government through regulatory stewardship.
contrary_evidence: A peer review is not a verdict on the government's overall safety record.
It does not show personal presidential control over the plant.

evidence.claim: Mexico announced the 2022 integrated external radiological emergency exercise near Laguna Verde as a preventive civil-protection measure in line with nuclear and radiological safety requirements.
evidence.title: Gobierno de México y gobierno de Veracruz anuncian simulacro en las inmediaciones de la Central Nucleoeléctrica Laguna Verde
evidence.excerpt: Mexico announced the 2022 integrated external radiological emergency exercise near Laguna Verde as a preventive civil-protection measure in line with nuclear and radiological safety requirements.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government release with a date and specific exercise description; the page itself was not fully retrievable here.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 period fit for emergency-preparedness context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect institutional attribution; it reflects the Mexican state apparatus under AMLO rather than a personal nuclear decision.
contrary_evidence: A drill is not evidence of a crisis or accident.
It is preparedness context, not direct proof of improved governance.

evidence.claim: Mexico welcomed the successful conclusion of the first TPNW meeting and framed itself as one of the treaty's architects with a tradition of nuclear disarmament leadership.
evidence.title: Conclusion of the first meeting of the Nuclear Weapons Ban Treaty in Vienna
evidence.excerpt: Mexico welcomed the successful conclusion of the first TPNW meeting and framed itself as one of the treaty's architects with a tradition of nuclear disarmament leadership.
evidence.source_locator: press release summary and opening paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official foreign-ministry release; the page was blocked but the indexed summary is clear and specific.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and relevant to nuclear-disarmament diplomacy.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State foreign-policy posture under AMLO; indirect but useful evidence of the government's alignment.
contrary_evidence: Treaty advocacy is not the same as operational safety governance.
It does not show any nuclear command authority because Mexico lacks nuclear weapons.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 evidence on AMLO's personal control over civilian-nuclear safety appointments, regulatory discipline, or command-side decisions is thin.
There is no Mexico-originating war, proxy conflict, or coercive peace leverage in 2022, so the dossier is mostly diplomatic posture rather than operational conflict conduct.
Specific chain-of-command evidence for some police, military, and intelligence abuses remains incomplete, especially for local versus federal responsibility.
Some of the evidence about electoral reform and media pressure is rhetorical or journalistic rather than a direct legal finding of intent to entrench power.
The causal split between AMLO policy, inherited weakness, and global shocks is still only partially recoverable for 2022 poverty, inflation, and investment outcomes.
Independent post-launch quality and outcome audits for IMSS-Bienestar, education recovery, and related welfare programs are thinner than the rollout record.
Direct documentary evidence of personal enrichment, hidden financial benefit, or knowing approval of surveillance remains limited.
Durability and post-launch independent audits for AIFA, Dos Bocas, IMSS-Bienestar, and the education programs are thinner than the implementation record.
